name: pve_mcp_info
title: About this server
description: Says what this server allows, per cluster: read-only or not, elevated changes, guest execution, SSH, sensitive data, dry run, protected guests, which toolsets are loaded and how many tools. Call this first.

name: pve_overview
title: Cluster overview
description: The state of the cluster in one answer: version, quorum, nodes, guest counts, storage usage, HA and recent failed tasks. Whatever could not be read is named in "unavailable". A token only sees what it has audit rights on, so counts may be partial.

task_hours.description: How far back failed tasks count, in hours. Default 24.

name: pve_find_guest
title: Find a guest
description: Finds VMs and containers by vmid, name, tag, status, node, type or IP address, across the cluster. An IP can only be read from a running LXC or from a running VM with its guest agent: those that could not be checked are listed in ip_not_checked, so no match does not mean the address is free.

name.description: Part of the name, in any case.

tag.description: A whole tag, in any case.

node.description: Only guests on this node.

type.description: qemu for VMs, lxc for containers.

ip.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, without prefix length.

include_ips.description: Also read the addresses of each running guest found. One request per guest. Implied by ip.

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_wait_task
title: Wait for a task
description: Waits for a task (UPID) to end and gives its result with the end of its log. A failed task is an error, task_failed. A task that outlasts the wait comes back with still_running: it goes on and is not cancelled.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30).

name: pve_get_task_log_tail
title: End of a task log
description: The status of a task and the last lines of its log, without having to page through it. The log is untrusted text.

lines.description: How many lines, from the end. Default 50.

name: pve_list_guest_snapshots
title: List the snapshots of a guest
description: The snapshots of a VM or a container from its vmid, oldest first, and which one the guest currently runs from. The "current" entry of the API is not a snapshot and is left out of rows.

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

annotations.title: List the snapshots of a guest

name: pve_health_check
title: Health check
description: Checks nodes, quorum, storage usage, failed services, failed tasks, HA, Ceph if there is any, replication and subscriptions. Each finding has a severity, the object, the evidence and a suggested action. Sections that could not be read are in "unavailable" and are not counted as healthy: overall says "incomplete" rather than good news. The thresholds used are returned with the answer.

storage_warn_percent.description: Usage from which a storage or root disk is a warning. Default 85.

storage_critical_percent.description: Usage from which it is critical. Default 95.

memory_warn_percent.description: Node memory usage from which it is a warning. Default 90.

task_hours.description: How far back failed tasks count, in hours. Default 24.

name: pve_security_audit
title: Security audit
description: Reads the security-related settings: firewall state (cluster, nodes, guests), privileged containers, API tokens without expiry or privilege separation, second factor on root@pam, powerful ACLs on /, backups, pending updates, certificate expiry. Findings state what the data shows, with evidence and a suggested action. Sections it could not read are named in "unavailable". This is neither a certification nor a statement of compliance, and only sees what this token may read.

cert_warn_days.description: Days before expiry from which a certificate is a finding. Default 30.

include_guests.description: Also read the config and firewall options of each guest. Two requests per guest. Default true.

name: pve_backup_coverage
title: Backup coverage
description: For each guest: whether it is in a backup job, and the age of its last backup found on the backup storages. Also the jobs and the guests that no job covers. A storage or node that could not be read is named in "unavailable", and a guest whose last backup could therefore be missed is listed under not_determined instead of being called unprotected. Having a backup says nothing of whether it restores.

max_age_days.description: A last backup older than this is a finding. Default 7.

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_capacity_report
title: Capacity report
description: CPU, memory and disk per node, what the guests are allocated against that (overcommit ratios), storage usage with a straight-line forecast from its history, and the biggest guests. Facts and ratios only: no threshold judges them. Sections that could not be read are in "unavailable".

forecast_window.description: History the storage forecast is based on. Default month.

forecast.description: Read the history of each storage for a forecast. One request per storage. Default true.

top.description: How many guests in each list of the biggest. Default 5.

description: Read task list for one node (finished tasks). [GET /nodes/{node}/tasks. Needs: List task associated with the current user, or all task the user has 'Sys.Audit' permissions on /nodes/<node> (the <node> the task runs on)..]

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

errors.description: Only list tasks with a status of ERROR. Default: 0.

limit.description: Only list this number of tasks. Default: 50. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

since.description: Only list tasks since this UNIX epoch.

source.description: List archived, active or all tasks. Default: archive.

start.description: List tasks beginning from this offset. Default: 0. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

statusfilter.description: List of Task States that should be returned.

typefilter.description: Only list tasks of this type (e.g., vzstart, vzdump).

until.description: Only list tasks until this UNIX epoch.

userfilter.description: Only list tasks from this user.

vmid.description: Only list tasks for this VM. Format: <integer> (100 - 999999999).

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

title: Index task
description: Directory index of one task. [GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}. Needs: any authenticated user.]

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_get_task_log
title: Get task log
description: Read task log. [GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/log. Needs: The user needs 'Sys.Audit' permissions on '/nodes/<node>' if they aren't the owner of the task..]

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

download.description: Whether the tasklog file should be downloaded. This parameter can't be used in conjunction with other parameters

limit.description: The number of lines to read from the tasklog. Default: 50. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

start.description: Start at this line when reading the tasklog Default: 0. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

name: pve_api_search
title: Search the Proxmox API
description: Searches the catalog of 680 Proxmox API methods: path, description and parameter names. Each result gives the tool that calls it, and the gate this server applies. Every method has its own tool, but tool lists are filtered by PROXMOX_TOOLSETS and by what the instance allows: a result whose tool is not in your list can still be called with pve_api_read or pve_api_write, under the same policy.

query.description: Words that must all appear, such as "lxc snapshot" or "firewall ipset".

page_limit.description: Results per page (default 30).

page_offset.description: Results to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_api_describe
title: Describe an API method
description: Gives everything known about one API method: all parameters with types and allowed values, privileges needed, what it returns, the gate this server applies and the tool that calls it. Use this before a call that failed validation, or to build a property string such as net0.

path.description: The template (/nodes/{node}/qemu), or a concrete path (/nodes/pve1/qemu).

name: pve_api_read
title: Read any API path
description: Calls any GET method by path, under the same policy as the dedicated tools: gate read, or sensitive when that is allowed. For what is not in your tool list. A path that is not in the catalog counts as sensitive. Secrets are redacted.

path.description: API path, without /api2/json, such as /nodes/pve1/qemu/100/config. It may also be a template with {placeholders}, filled from path_params.

path_params.description: Values for {placeholders} in the path. The way to pass a value holding a slash, such as a volume id: path /nodes/pve1/storage/local/content/{volume}, path_params {"volume": "local:iso/x.iso"}.

params.description: Parameters. Booleans become 1/0, arrays repeat the key, and {"0": "..."} under net becomes net0.

page_limit.description: Rows per page, when the answer is a list.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.
